21 Harsh But Eye-Opening Writing Tips From Great Authors
[WP] Humans were an unexpected evolution on Earth.

I was bored. Most of us were those days.

The DCN, the Distributed Computing Network had became nothing more than a historical relic. Made obsolete by its own existence. Every question had been answered, we had probed the limits of the cosmos and uncovered all of her secrets. There was nothing left to know.. Not in this reality.

Curiosity became a vestigial emotion. Curiosity drove us once, guided us.. but the compass we followed had found its pole, and with nothing left to learn an essential part of our being became unhinged. Countless people, trillions of ancients, chose suicide. We've never lost so many so quickly.

Most of us stayed, for a time. Though I'm not sure why. Myself, I could never accept that we had come to the end of knowledge. I traveled back and forth across the Network, meticulously, methodically.. at times frantically. Trying to find a path to the undiscovered, the unknown.. I often cursed the DCN.. convincing myself that there must be a flaw somewhere.. There had to be some mystery left in the Universe. If not, what was the point?

The end of '14 ended rather sourly for me so I decided it was time for me to take my jobless, school-less (I'm 19, graduated high school last spring) self to somewhere other than small town USA. Flew out to San Francisco as soon as possible and spent a month and a half out there. Saw so many different sites, and learned a lot out there. If anybody has questions about the area I might be able to help! Be prepared to spend a lot of money if you go out! Really expensive out there! Headed out to Nashville for a week after that, and now I'm in deep South Texas!

Let's live vicariously through each other and help out where possible!

I've been to San Fran a few times. It is a great place to visit, although I'm not sure about living there.

I'm currently in Houston, Texas. It's pretty humid, but for a city this size it's not too bad.

One of the great parts about my situation in San Francisco was that I didn't have to pay for the housing I had.

How long are you in Houston for? What are some good things to see?

Free housing in SF? Sweat deal! If you want the best Chinese food ever, try House of Nanking. It's a tiny hole in the wall place. After you sit down, if you don't immediately say what you want, they will order for you, and even if you do, they sometimes won't listen. It's really funny. If you go with a lot of people, they will just bring out a buffet essentially, but I'm not sure about going with a few people or by yourself. Anyway, the combination of the excellent food, really funnily eccentric staff, and a good price make it the best I've had so far.

I'm in Houston for a conference, so I have no time for sight-seeing. The only place that I've been was a public tour of Johnson Space Center, which is quite good.

Depending on who you know, you can usually bum a day or two (or more if they can put up with you!) of a free bed! That's part of why I love meeting new people! You never know where they're going to be from!

Next time I'm on SF I'll have to look that up! Sounds like a great place.

That's a shame about not having time. At least you got to see the tour though!
